tips.comment: Dark Shore can be opposed here given Dark Angel’s 5% SR (A/E 0.29) with 2yo colt debutants in C1-3 races and 18% SR (A/E 0.48) with 2yo colt debutants when favourite. Words Of Truth must do better than an 5l defeat on debut at Newbury in May, but this is also a marked step up in class so you can’t be confident. NEW MONARCH makes plenty of appeal to me at 10/3; the son of Acclamation gave a promising display FTO at Newbury last month but just failed to see out the 6.5f. He’s got 1/2f less to contend with here for a yard who are excelling with their 2yo’s on their 2nd start (27% SR, A/E 1.26), and owner Teme Valley Racing’s 28% SR (A/E 1.71) with sprinters adds further confidence.

Words of Truth, a 2-year-old chestnut gelding with Charlie Appleby. 2025, 16th May. Made his debut at Newbury, drifted in the betting, and was given a very educational introduction here. Followed the horse and was not given much daylight, ran on under a very tender ride. Will come on a bundle for this run.
Rebels Romance to cause a stir here. Ran very well and is on a hat-trick bid. Beat Al Riffa, who has gone and won again. Step up to Group 1 but thriving now.
Likes it around here and has run well here. Massively unlucky here in the Britannia where he got no luck in running. Comes here off the same mark and is the one to beat.

Aalto almost won the Bunbury Cup at Newmarket two years running, finishing well into 2nd, losing by a nose. He also ran in this race last year behind Northern Express but never had a chance after a poor start. He should do better this time with William Buick booked.

A real lack of pace again could play to Northern Express' chances having won this last year from a mark 2lbs higher. High draw this year but looks to be the right side and cheekpieces are retained. Ran well two starts back to finish 7th at Royal Ascot and can repeat the feat from last year in similar conditions.

Backing Billyjoh, the 5-year-old grey gelding by Mayson trained by Michael Appleby, in tomorrow’s prestigious Moët & Chandon International Handicap (Heritage Handicap, Class 2, 7f) at Ascot. He’s a horse long overdue a big performance, and with conditions, form, and jockey all aligning, he looks primed to deliver.
Billyjoh hasn’t won on turf since his debut, but his record includes solid placings in top handicaps??'most notably second in the Buckingham Palace Stakes over C&D at Royal Ascot 2024, plus a third at Newmarket in the Bunbury Cup two weeks ago where he showed pace and fight in a hot 7f handicap.
Rated 94 and now 1 lb below last year’s Ascot mark, Billyjoh looks well treated. He has run consistently this season??'four seconds and four thirds from 12 starts, often in big fields and strong races??'so fitness is clearly not an issue.

Hasn't finished out of the first four in four outings so far this season. Made all to win at Sandown last time out over a mile. Has won over today's trip and goes on any ground. Looks a solid selection for each way betting with many bookies paying out on extra places.

As always this is a very tough handicap, with one or two that will progress to pattern company in due course in the field. The Ed Bethall trained Yorkshire looks a fair each way price, and should run a good race. He ran a very nice race in the Buckingham Palace Handicap at the Royal meeting, after a short break. He is quite well treated with those that re-oppose here, so theoretically he should go close. His draw is probably the main negative, as a few places higher would have helped.

Has a good record here and mark is ok, shame the 2lb cut wasn't already off. Going to take this 18-1 now as i think it reprents good ew value and will be surprised if it goes up much, if at all. Has won this race before in 2022 (off 98) and was 3rd last year, so expecting a good run.

Race 4 at Ascot today is the Moet & Chandon International Handicap (Class 2) for 3-year-olds and upwards over 1,408 m and has attracted a large field of 22 runners. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 5-year-old gelding Oliver Show from the George Boughey yard and will be ridden by Billy Loughnane. This son of No Nay Never is wearing blinkers for the first time today. He is a useful sort and still has plenty of scope for improvement. One can safely draw a line through his latest effort as he has been a very consistent sort and did not have a clear run in that race either. Big chance today and must not be excluded from anything.

Hasn't really shown any form so far as a 4-year-old but ran up a hat trick of wins around this time in 2024. Needs to settle better, and although he needs to step up, he has the talent to place at least.

Generally, just be mid to high, midfield or more forward, and you can go well here over CD. But with a genuine lack of pace here, this looks a fairly fraught affair. As a result, I’m going to take a bit of a stab and sidestep the above for a chance on Array on handicap debut. Whilst a mark of 102 is seemingly 2 lbs above a future mark of 100, he has been finishing in and around horses rated plenty higher. A look at his family would suggest he’s been a disappointment so far, but with entries over a mile, and a Group 2 entry retained, there must be some hope he can go well on handicap debut. He just looks worth chancing at the odds to me outside of the interconnected form lines of the others that make this muddling, and this race has been won from a low draw extreme on occasion, so stall 2 doesn’t overly concern as a result. Any repeat of his Newbury 3rd on seasonal debut can see him involved if he can cope with the weight carry.

Only 1-18 and no win since handicap debut, but has run well in some decent sprint handicaps and posted solid placed efforts at Doncaster and Newmarket since upped to 7 furlongs. Needs more to land a big pot like this, but it would be no surprise to see him run well at a price.

Winless since his 2yo days, but hinted at a return to form with a respectable effort at Sandown last time. The drop back to 1m looks a positive move given past performances, and while his Australian campaign in 2024 didn't come to much he's showing some encouraging signs. Not the most consistent, but not without hope at 25/1 and 6 places on offer.

Race 7 at Ascot today is a Handicap (Class 4) for 3-year-olds and upwards over 2,405 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 3-year-old gelding Criminal from the Richard Hughes yard, and will be ridden by current leading jockey William Buick. This son of Sea The Moon is well handicapped here and is trying this distance for the first time. He has given the impression that he needs more ground on his first three runs when running on late in all. If he is good enough, he will win here under the polished William Buick.

Was another that was a strong fancy last time but was outpaced before rallying late on so looks a good move taking another step up in trip. Looked a bit quirky last time and is understandable blinkers are slapped on in place of the cheek pieces but has ability and dropped 2lb must go close. Not certain to stay on pedigree but went straight into my notebook last time with the remark 'Next time over further' so have to go in again based on what my fading old eyes told me. Steps up in grade as well as trip but yard going well enough ( 3 winners from last 10 sent out) and if taking to the blinkers has to go very close.

8 runners here and 3-year-olds are the target choices. The selection has improved the further up in trip it's gone and is off a lowly 69 today. Billy is on board, and I can see this being a Williams special. Although the favorite 'could be anything.'
A beaten favourite over 6 furlongs at Newcastle last time out and trying this 5 furlong trip for the first time. Ryan Moore takes the reins back today which looks a positive sign.

Connections of Tropical Storm were a bit too ambitious last time when they ran him in a Group 1 at Ascot, and he ended up well beaten. The run before that, he was successful in a Listed race, and now dropped down into a handicap, he looks the one to beat.

Made good efforts in these Class 2 sprints this year. 5th out of 19 in the Epsom Dash last month, a nose 2nd out of 14 at Newcastle last time out. Both runs were under today's in-form 5lb claimer. Mid draw could be handy.

I'm still kicking myself for not backing Flowerhead at massive odds at Royal Ascot last time as had backed her at Chepstow and she went into the notebook. However Midnight Tango is another noted after last time giving me a real fright by nearly reeling in my backed horse Argentine Tango. On one line of form through that one and another horse Shine On Me she has a similar chance to Flowerhead so at the prices looks the value bet here especially as she had some of these behind last time and looks a proper improver. Holds a 7f Group 1 entry and half brother is a mile winner so might want further in time but if getting a strong pace to aim at looks a cracking bet as should finish strongly and hit the frame at the very least. Yard going well and had a 2yo winner at Ascot on Friday and this one looks a massive play for me today. I do like Flowerhead but at double the price I'll side with this one with the four places sure to yield a return.
She looks to be capable of scoring again in this, despite carrying a penalty for her win at Beverley at the start of this month over 5f. The extra furlong should help her.

Aleezdancer has won 7 times, including over course and distance last May off the same mark as today. After being unplaced in his next 6 starts, he bounced back to form at Pontefract two weeks ago when leading throughout. His best form is on soft ground, so with showers forecast, he looks like a good each-way bet with 6 places on offer.

Kept on well when 8th of 23 over this trip in the Wokingham at Royal Ascot last time out despite being slow away. He managed to finish second of seven in his group and is eased 2 pounds in the ratings for each-way appeal.

Strike Red loves York having only run one bad race here in 5 visits and that under a different jockey. Finished 0.75L to Elmonjed at the Ebor meeting over C&D last August and 9lbs better off with that rival here (likely fav) whilst a high draw looks good with Sargeant Wilko going forward from stall 22. A mark of 93 has seen him win in the past and conditions are in his favour to go well again at a track he loves.

Backing Sergeant Wilko, the 4-year-old Bungle Inthejungle gelding trained by Kevin Ryan, in the highly competitive Sky Bet Dash at York. Despite not winning this term, he remains dangerous off a mark of 94??'95, and boasts five wins from 16 starts, including stakes success at Goodwood, Newmarket, and Leicester last season.
This year, he has posted consistent turf handicaps: 4th at Haydock (May 31), 4th at Newcastle (May 11), and 5th at Newcastle (June 28), all over 6f and performing creditably off similar marks??'confirming race fitness and consistent form.
Sergeant Wilko is a York winner in Class 2 sprint company (Oct 2024) and handles soft ground well, having won and placed on that going previously??'ideal given tomorrow’s forecast. In a 22-runner, high-tempo handicap, expect jockey Tom Eaves to settle him just off the pace before unleashing his strong late run along the Knavesmire straight. Given his profile and the likely pace setup, he offers attractive each-way value at around 22/1.
I'm hoping this prolific winner will be fit enough after a break. The jockey claims seven, and the yard's in form. Each way advised, just in case he needs it.

Risky tip so it's just a small each-way chance , the good odds are the main reason for this tip, extra places available each-way this race. Finished 8th of 8 last time out which was over 7f , drops back in trip today which is possibly more suitable. Today is just his 2nd run back from a rest so maybe he improves for that last run, better shape fitness wise today. Already has some good form in the book in some good races over this sort of distance , that form gives him a small chance today , very very small each-way tip.

A fairly wild stab at this handicap with Orne, who clearly will take some forgiving in general for his lack of consistency. He’s down the weights though, and notably in the context of this race he did give 10 lbs to Rousing Encore back in April and only got beaten a length. With that horse 12/1 for this, and Orne getting a 13 lb swing in the weights, I felt like a small case could be made. His record at 6f on fairer tracks reads better than his form anywhere else, with a peak effort splitting Inisherin and Vandeek clearly reading well in the context of a mark of 84. 0/8 over 6f doesn’t fill you with confidence, but I just feel like he’s got to go in at some point, and the drop in trip onto a straight 6 and a career low weight carry could combine for a better effort. At the very least, the negatives are massively baked into his price.
Throw a dart, small stakes, bit of fun. But Nazron ran well in a 0-90 last time out and should give this a go. Chances to hit the frame.
Interesting form with not hitting the frame, but this horse is so due a win soon. When it's ready, it will be ready. Bit disappointed with the price, but have to take it.

Three runs this year for the 5-year-old, a decent return run and excuses in two subsequent races. He’s a previous 5f C/D winner. Won or placed in 13 races. Plenty of nice runs last year and high RPR ratings posted. Down to an attractive mark now.

Yet to win for Tim Easterby but has been running fairly consistently since arriving from Ollie Sangster and posted another decent effort when 2nd at Ripon last time. Dropped a lb for that so should be in the mix once again.
Mudamer looks the way to go. Staying on strongly last time out, need a horse like that to finish strongly today. Good chance to hit the frame.

Bowood could be one to run well from an each-way angle, i like the current odds. Better effort and a sign of a return to form when finishing 3rd last time out, a slow start really didn't help otherwise may have done better but did show enough to be worth considering today. Ground conditions might not be as quick today as they were last time which may well be more suitable for Bowood. Today's NAP selection , very small each-way chance.

Secret Mistral has improved recently, and his good second at Haydock was followed by a win there. On both occasions, he made all, and with being drawn 2 here, he has a good chance of repeating it. The small penalty shouldn't hinder the progress in a thin race.

Not helped by the draw but has shaped as though conditions here could be close to optimal. The trainer doesn't come to the track often and has a great record when he does. Pace could also be strong assuming no further withdrawals, which would suit. Looks interesting.
Back down into an easier grade than when running 6th out of 14 last time out. Should be able to take this if getting the splits.

Ran very well on debut at a big price. Has Cosgrove on board again, and I can see it going one better. Slight drift with plenty of money for the Johnston horse, but that needs to find some improvement. Whereas a repeat run for the selection should win.

He was last on his debut over the same trip in May at Haydock, but that was in a higher class. Also, the winner that day has gone on to place in a group race. His breeding suggests that there is improvement to be had, and why not show it today?
Has the draw here to make an effort. Is unexposed along with Mandanda and should do very well, at least making the frame.

I think he has his conditions tomorrow. That is Class 4 over 7 furlongs, under which he has 3 wins and 2 places from 6 runs. The trainer is in form, and the jockey has won on him, so he looks a cracking each way at the price.

Andrew Balding's Brighton Boy made a decent seasonal debut when finishing seventh over seven furlongs at Goodwood in May, and was then the subject of a considerable gamble, 25/1 into 7/1, in the Palace Of Holyroodhouse Stakes over the minimum trip at the Royal Meeting where he finished very disappointingly last of the 24 runners. Back up to six furlongs here should suit him a lot better.

Andesite, a 3-year-old bay gelding. This will be only his second run in a handicap - down one pound after running well to finish 6th at Newmarket. Drawn in stall 3 here at Chester - a low draw is always an advantage. Looks a nice each-way price.
Has a good draw and is carrying considerably less weight today. Should give this a go against higher graded horses. Chances.

3-year-olds are the order today. With the allowance, this looks a solid bet, and I expected 2/1 rather than the odds on offer. Added to the jockey allowance for a good jockey, great bet. Flickering Halo the saver.
Made all when winning over half a furlong shorter at Epsom 9 days ago, and well drawn in stall 1 to take them all along from the front again.
Just failed at Pontefract last time out in a hot race. Should take the beating today if getting a clear run. Big player.
Duran, a 4-year-old bay gelding. Plum draw in one for this 5-furlong race. Always a big bonus to be drawn low.

Scored at Lingfield in March but has failed to build on that, finishing well held on both starts since. Now returns from a short break and will be fine at the trip and on the ground. Capable on his day and has a very capable claimer.

This is a pretty open race with some younger unexposed types with little to recommend them. The selection is a C&D winner and has recently been running on the AW, on which he has a poor record. Prior to that, he ran well at Leicester and Doncaster over this trip. Now 7lbs lower than his last winning mark, I think he is a decent bet at the price.
Should give this a go. Ran on one pace last time out, 2 furlongs less. Bold bid expected with the longer trip to suit. Chances of the places.
Cloudside Rock, a 4-year-old bay colt, is down to his lowest ever handicap mark here, and he hasn't been running too badly. Looks like an interesting each-way punt.
Three difficult starts to date, but I think fortunes will change now. Handicapping, especially off the starting mark, which is with a 3lb claimer, has a chance if he can handle going up in trip.
This gelding looks well worth a bet. He's won at the course off higher marks, and he likes the ground. The draw's not ideal, but the price compensates.

La Pulga is generally quite consistent, and usually tries hard. He ran well in a better race at Ascot last time, and is well suited to the Tapeta surface here at Newcastle. I expect him to set the pace, and if he doesn't get taken on for the lead, can finish off strongly to record another winner for the in form Charlie Johnston team.

Has a track record of 2/4/1/1/2 at Newcastle, 1 over today’s distance and the other when taking his last win in November 2024 (1m2f) when running off a mark 68.
Although running off a mark of 74 today, he has shown decent form in his 4 runs to date in 2025, all ran off the same mark of 74, including a run over 1m2f at Newcastle when beaten 4 lengths into 2nd (of 7) having been short of room over 1f out, so I reckon a return to AW today after 3 turf outings could see him outrun his current odds of 10.00

This gelding usually runs over jumps and is decent. He's making his flat handicap debut today with Adam Wedge the jump jockey aboard and he can go very close. The yard are going well and he's had a breathing op.
Won over the distance last time out at Carlisle. Up five pounds for that win, still looks well treated today. Ground conditions today will suit. Stable going well, should be hard to beat.
Loves it here and a hat-trick bid is looming. Has the draw on the rail and should power up if taking it. Big player again.

I love to think Beraz can come home in front, but he has a long losing spell to overcome. Whereas my selection is on an attractive mark. He is twice a course and distance winner off marks of 77 & 80, and with Mason Paetel taking off 5lb, today's mark stands out at 77. Last seen 45 days ago after a 54-day absence, he finished a decent 3rd of 7 in a race where the form has been franked since.

Won a 1m Maiden in his 4th career run and although he showed little in his next 4 runs, on switching to handicaps, he finally came good in his last run, 19 days ago, having dropped 7lbs from his opening handicap mark to finish 2 lengths of 12 in a 1m, Class 6 handicap.
He has gone up 1lb for his latest run, but stepping up in grade for today’s run has him receiving weight from all but 1 of the 11 runner field, so if handling the surface on making his AW debut today, he could run a big race at big odds if running to the level of his latest runner up finish
Berkshire Phantom to go in again here. Found its winning pattern last time out, and this is a winnable race. Brunello Breeze is the danger.

Has a cracking record of 3 wins from 5 runs here and drops snugly 4 lbs below his last winning mark with the good claimer's allowance coming off. This is his first run for Liam Bailey but is an intelligent bit of placing, and he showed enough at Haydock in May after another break to encourage.

4-year-old gelding now appears to be heading in the right direction and looks unexposed in the lineup here this afternoon. He ran well last time, finishing 6th out of 13 at Ayr at the start of the month, setting off at 40/1. Can improve on that today.
Ran on well inside the final furlong over this trip at Beverley 11 days ago, and every chance to go one better remaining on the same mark.
If it can get the rail run ahead of New York State of Mind, it should have every chance to win. If not, at least get in the top 4.
On opposite sides today, the two favorites, and that should be enough for Mr. Heinz to get the better of the favorite this time, player.

This is a fairly desperate looking affair, however Elettaria makes some appeal on recent form, and having shown a liking for this surface. She isn't quick, and usually gets behind, however I could see her finishing better than most.
Just 2 wins from 22 runs makes for grim reading and currently in poor form, but much better on AW and has performed well at this course in the past, so not ready to rule him out.

Lahina Bay is dropping in the weights and generally running well, so I think there's every chance she lands a race of this type before too long. Looks capable and bound to give us a run for our money.
Ran green from 3 out but kept on inside the final furlong over a furlong further at Lingfield last time out and could appreciate this drop in trip.

Generally has been running on the all-weather, albeit not very well with just the one win at Kempton. Made debut for new stable on a little bit of form, finishing 2nd at Leicester after two months off the track. Wind surgery at the beginning of the year did show a slight improvement, and perhaps both together could see a first win since March 2024.

Excellent each-way value at 16/1 and makes a stable debut after a lengthy layoff. Promise in last season's nursery run and with Kingscote off to Hong Kong soon I feel the booking could be significant. Could well be in the mix.
Shaped well on turf debut on penultimate start under today's jockey, just needing the run, before disappointing last time. Eased in grade here, is worth another chance dropped a pound.

Consistent filly who dug deep to win here two starts ago over 5f, just 2lbs higher now and shaped better than bare result back here over 5f last time out. Runs over 6f for the first time, and that could bring about further improvement in a pretty weak contest that doesn't need much, if any, improvement to win.
No comment made

Has an eye-catching pedigree, being out of a useful dam and half-sister to Group 1 winning sprinter The Tin Man. Sired by Gregorian so there is hope for speed and ability in this competitive introduction.
Was running over 5 furlongs in its last race after a break. Stepping back up to 6 furlongs will suit. Has won here before.
Has the highest mark in this field but is not currently in good form. No wins from 17 runs, and it helps that he has experience over C&D. Being 3lbs lighter than the LTO mark should help.
Desert Treasure defied a slow start at Yarmouth last week to come clear by 1.25 lengths. She will have learned a lot from that and looks likely to follow up.
No comment made

This is such a weak race that I can't resist a small bet on this one, which was ahead of horses rated around 10 lb higher than her last time out. This extra trip looks sure to suit. The real key for me, though, is the first-time booking of a very promising apprentice who is able to claim 7 lb. The stable is very shrewd, so his booking looks highly significant to me. The horse won't get many better opportunities than this bottom-of-the-basement race, where she's less exposed than many of the others.

After running a close second in his previous two races over five furlongs on good to firm and good ground, this W J Haggas-trained 3-year-old gelding won his latest race over six furlongs on good to firm ground at Newmarket 30 days ago. He ran on strongly inside the final furlong to beat the Mrs R Carr-trained Fiscal Policy by a cozy 1 1/2 lengths. With Cieren Fallon back in the plate, another win looks more than likely.

Decent each-way chance in this. His mark is one he can win from, down a pound from last time where a line can be put through that run. He won his maiden over course and distance on penultimate start, a race which has had several winners come out of it since.

Was still learning when winning here in April off 71 and has run creditably since, including a close fourth beaten 2 1/2 lengths off 77. Handicapper may still have his grip but Ashley Lewis claims 7lb.
Started his debut in impressive style by winning at Salisbury last July. But the switch to handicaps has not gone to plan just yet. Hoping the 3rd attempt now with a dropped mark does the trick.
Addison Grey should win this one with ease in a very weak-looking race. It has by far the best form, judging by its winning debut at Southwell last November.
Lost Signal, a 2-year-old chestnut colt, was 3rd at Newbury on debut. We can expect another bold showing here from this Richard Hannon inmate.
Trainer in good form. Selection placed on both his turf runs last year before having excuses on his reappearance run on AW in April. Looks to have been given a generous mark to start handicapping.
Crystal Mariner, a 5-year-old chestnut gelding. Back in trip and down in the handicap, worth taking a chance with Saffie Osbourne back on board.

Gelded son of Earthlight & Adutchgirl ( Dam's sire Dutch Art ) who was last seen at Leicester 9 days ago where finishing 2nd/8 that was his best performance yet and arrives here having found the excellent opportunity to go a place better and shed that maidan tag here as this race should be run to suit given the horses enrolled to run here and this race is not as competitive as it may seem at a quick glance of the form book steps up in trip here racing at the full 1 mile trip for the first that being a good move by his connections as this trip can help bring out more improvement and he is open to plenty of progress at this stage and this trip is well worth exploring currently operating on an unchanged mark of 55 P Attwater's inmate looks poised to strike here with jockey Jack Callan taking off a very valuable looking 7lb which only enhances his good looking claims here merits serious consideration in a race of this nature
Jet Black would have been the likely winner last time out but swerved to her left when leading 1f from the finish. She should do better in this 4-runner field and is the worthy favorite.
Looks a good chance to get off the mark here. Guarded was disappointing last time out, so won't risk that again. Big player here.
Take this to come out on top in this race, as it had previously run only to be blocked last time. With a clear passage, it should take the beating here.
Decent third at Down Royal last time and has been placed in listed company previously. Has enough ability to take this.

Heather might be the one to beat here. The selection has had solid form figures all season and was runner-up over a longer trip at Down Royal last time. This track will be better suited and can run a big race.
This decent filly goes up in trip after a luckless run last time. The yard is in better form, so she can go close.

Drama Queen has a nice pedigree by Wootton Bassett and runs for trainer Donnacha O'Brien (SR 32%) in familiar dark silks for big name Ballydoyle owners. Improved possibly for the step up in trip on third maiden start and worked hard to win. Could go well in an intriguing Listed contest over 1m4f.

Famous Enough is still a maiden after 15 starts, but there has been promise in some recent runs. He had been poor in his first 11 starts but showed his first sign of ability here at Gowran over 8 furlongs in May when 5th, beaten just 2.5 lengths. He followed that with 3rd of 15 over the same course and distance two weeks later. His last start was equally as good, finishing 4th of 20 at Leopardstown 2 weeks ago. He is off the same mark here, but his apprentice rider claims 7lbs, so he looks like a good EW bet with 4 places on offer.

The second division of the apprentice handicap isn't the strongest of races. Serafina is interesting, running for Dermot Weld. Off a long time until the recent comeback run (not really backed there over 1 mile, soft ground, and not really asked many questions either). These conditions are more similar to those the Profitable mare (by Galileo mare) won under previously. 7lbs claimer Conor Cusack has begun well with 3 wins from 11 rides. Could be up to this on the second start back from a lengthy absence for the top yard.

TOMAHAWK KING needs to bounce back from a poor run latest , but he is effective at this venue and the stiff finish will suit. He is one of much the best treated runners lining up in this weak looking division of this split handicap and at these early odds second-up this spell his wellbeing is worth taking on trust.
The race is full of inexperienced horses and plenty who have not run as yet. Tahcawin ran in a decent maiden last time where it finished well and should find this race much easier.

Lake Swan is a 2yo filly trained by Gavin Cromwell (3-2-2 yesterday with runners). She made an encouraging debut at Navan at 13-2. 'Towards rear against far rail, headway into midfield halfway, keeping on when hampered over 1f out, not recover (op 8/1)' and was beaten 9.25l. Owned by Ben Halsall, who has sent out another 2yo filly, Quiet Mutiny, trained again by Gavin Cromwell, and it won on debut earlier this month. Quiet Mutiny won a 15-runner maiden at Fairyhouse and didn't go unfancied - 9-2 into 3-1f, beating an A P O'Brien filly called Precise, who holds three Group race entries. Lake Swan may have needed that run but will surely come on for the debut run and is likely to be a lot better than we have seen so far.
Big chances here. Ran very well last time out and is unexposed. Should give a good go with the same weight as last time. Big field but chances.
Sierra De Gredos was only just beaten last time and was a previous winner at this course three races ago. It looks like it's got what it takes to win this.

Mullacash Buzz is a 7-year-old gelding trained by Thomas Dowling. He has 6 wins out of 44 and has an inferior OR on turf of 44 compared to 56 on AW. That being said, Mullacash Buzz has won twice on turf at Naas off 55 and Roscommon off 61 with both wins coming on todays good groundd, so he is clearly well handicapped on his best form. He often races prominently or even leads in the majority of his races and has the capable Gavin Ryan on board. Mullacash Buzz was noticeably strong in the market on his last start, having been bet into 7-2 from an opening 10-1, which suggests this gelding is capable of re-entering the winner's enclosure with conditions being optimal.
Eric Lock was well beaten on the all-weather last time under a claiming rider, but is respected with a senior jockey back on board.
A change of trainer but jockey is familiar could spark a revival for Big Baby Bull who has seen his rating tumble dramatically. Unsure how he'll handle more rain but he's well weighted in this race.

An open-looking handicap where Amanirenas has dropped to a very attractive mark and looks great each-way value at 20/1 with 5 places up for grabs. He ran well last time at Bellestown despite losing ground out wide. This drop back in trip looks a big plus.

James The Second’s 15 of 15 over 6f LTO is a bit of a concern. But if we draw a line through that, the picture looks much better. He’s been 2nd twice this season (once here at Gowran), both over today’s trip of 7f, off this mark and 1lb below. They’ve added the first-time blinkers. Wesley Joyce takes over from 7lb claimer Terry Casey. Placed on good and heavy suggests he’ll handle any surface. 20/1 is fair, and I’ll have a small each-way poke.

Jawhary has only one win in his 32 starts, though that did come here at Gowran Park back in June 2021. He has run some good races this year, being placed in 3 of his 7 starts. He was 3rd of 18 over today's trip at Fairyhouse in June, and off the same mark with Sam Coen claiming 4 lbs, he looks like a good EW bet with 4 places on offer.
Comes here from a falling mark, now down to 54. He was placed on turf off this mark last September and won on AW from a 3lb higher mark in November. Worth an EW punt.

Dazzling Spirit ran pretty well when third over course and distance on first start for this stable back in April. The 7yo mare is very well handicapped on her best form (winner off ORs 62 and 63 in the past, runs off a rating of 40 today and apprentice claims 7lbs). Sent off 7-2 favourite with Colin Keane up on penultimate start. Better drawn today in stall 7. Has claims.
